title: Harris County Funds Independent Investigation; ICE Refuses to Name Agents
excerpt: Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare announced an independent criminal investigation into the ICE shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, citing the unprecedented refusal of federal authorities to share evidence or identify the agents involved.
content:
One week after the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by an ICE agent in Houston, Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare and Commissioner Rodney Ellis held a joint press conference to announce the county would fund its own independent criminal investigation.

Teare called the federal government's lack of cooperation 'unacceptable and unprecedented,' noting that in a typical officer-involved shooting, the DA's office knows the officer's identity within 12 hours — yet six days after the shooting, local investigators still did not know the names of the ICE agents present. 'We're almost a week in, and no one on the state level knows who they were or where they are right now. That's unacceptable,' Teare said.

  • The Harris County DA said his office would 'investigate it like we do all criminal investigations' and was 'good at identifying individuals who don't want to be found.'
  • Commissioner Ellis stated: 'We cannot ask the public to take ICE or DHS at their word and simply accept the account of the various agencies involved.'
  • The Texas Rangers confirmed they had not been asked to participate by any federal or local authority and were not involved in the investigation.
  • CNN reported that local Houston officials said federal investigators had 'shut them out' of the ongoing investigation entirely.
